acceptance_criteria: [x] Dedicated codex/0.2-wayback-ledger branch and NagiOS-0.2-wayback worktree from latest DF-01.
[x] DF-01 registration, ownership paths, dependency, state, gate, resume, verify, and handoff are accurate.
[x] Versioned activity entry includes stable ID, timestamp, actor, action, target, transaction, causal/correlation links, summary, metadata, reversibility, integrity, and schema version.
[x] Generic actor/principal and provenance model references external identities without duplicating Capability identity or policy.
[x] Versioned transaction lifecycle preserves ordered entries, begin/commit/abort/partial-failure semantics, and atomicity expectation.
[x] Reversibility distinguishes exact reversible work, compensation, snapshot-required work, irreversible work, and unknown work.
[x] Versioned restore point and snapshot manifest/reference contracts include scope, ledger boundary, integrity, compatibility, and parent/reference metadata.
[x] Append/query ledger supports time, actor, app/principal, target, action, transaction, correlation/cause, reversibility, and restore-point filters with ordered traversal and serialization.
[x] Append integrity verification detects modified, reordered, or truncated ledger data and does not silently accept mismatch.
[x] Privacy contract keeps payloads out by default and represents sensitive, redacted, omitted, unavailable, and snapshot-backed data.
[x] Versioned restore planning resolves dependencies and reports affected scopes, compatibility failures, irreversible/unknown blockers, and executable state without executing restore.
[x] Missing required snapshots and unsafe actions always make plans non-executable with explicit blocker reasons.
[x] Recent committed transactions derive undo candidates and distinguish exact undo, compensation, and snapshot requirements.
[x] Snapshot-store interface and deterministic in-memory metadata fixture resolve snapshot dependencies without copying filesystem contents.
[x] Unknown serialization versions and malformed metadata are rejected; migration policy is documented.
[x] Unit tests cover the requested IDs, transaction states, provenance, reversibility, snapshots, restore points, queries, serialization, integrity, and privacy negatives.
[x] Integration scenarios A-D cover reversible app actions, an AI causal chain, snapshot-backed restore planning, and unsafe restore rejection.
[x] Focused tests, regression tests, fmt, Clippy, JSON Schema validation, and ./nagi dev verify pass.
[x] No filesystem/runtime connection, actual restore executor, or M17/M18-M30 change is introduced.
[x] No Activity/Wayback UI, App SDK, Capability policy, or other native app workstream is changed.
[x] State and handoff record verified evidence, deferred hooks, dependency boundary, and exact next step.
[x] Final worktree is clean and changes are committed and pushed to the dedicated remote branch.
deferred: Filesystem change hook: not available before the M30 plus explicit 0.2 integration gate; future adapter accepts opaque object/version references and records metadata only, with acceptance proving append/query/provenance and snapshot-required planning without copying content into the ledger.

App-state hook: App SDK/app-state contract is owned elsewhere; future adapter records external app/session IDs and snapshot references, with acceptance proving app-scoped restore plans and no dependency on app-private APIs.

AI/tool action hook: AI runtime/tool contracts are owned elsewhere; future adapter supplies generic actor, initiating-event, parent/correlation, and transaction references, with acceptance proving the full causal chain and denials remain attributable.

Snapshot backend: this stream defines SnapshotStore and metadata-only fixtures; a durable guest backend requires filesystem ownership and the integration gate, with acceptance proving digest/manifest validation and missing-reference failure.

Restore executor: intentionally absent; future adapter consumes only executable plans after capability/policy checks and must log restore as a new reversible activity, with negative acceptance for stale, missing, incompatible, irreversible, and unknown inputs.

Wayback/Activity UI: owned by first-party app workstreams; future consumer renders transaction/action groups and explicit blockers from the public contract, with acceptance showing no fake undo for non-executable plans.

Capability/principal lookup: identity and authority remain externally owned; future adapter resolves opaque IDs and permissions without granting or strengthening rights, with permission-denial and missing-principal acceptance.
